div.head: III Atr 1.2
div.ab: Et pax que dabitur in unius burgi þincþa, emendetur VI hund'; et ubi dabitur in wapentako, emendetur infracta pax I hundreto; et pax que dabitur in ealahus, emendetur de homine occiso sex dimidiis marcis, de uiuo duodecim oris.

And þæt grið, þæt man sylleð on I burhgaþinðe, bete man þæt mid VI hundr; and þær man sylle on wǽpentáke, bete man þæt mid hundr, gif hit man brecð; and þæt man sylle on éalahuse, bete man þæt æt deadum menn mid VI healfmarce ⁊ æt cwicon mid XII óran.

And þæt grið þæt man sylleð on I burhgaþinðe, bete man þæt mid VI hund ̅r and þæ[t] man sylle on wǽpentáke, bete man þæt mid hund ̅r, gif hit man brecð; and þæt man sylle on éalahuse, bete man þæt æt deadum menn mid VI healfmarce ⁊ æt cwicon mid XII óran.

And for the breach of peace established in the court of one borough, 600 [of silver] shall be paid as compensation, and 100 for that established in a wapentake, In the case of breach of the peace in an ale-house, 6 half-marks shall be paid as compensation if a man is slain, and 12 ores if no-one is slain.

And the peace which is given in the meeting of one borough is to be atoned for with six hundred; and that which is given in a wapentake, is to be atoned for with a hundred, if it is broken; and that which is given in an alehouse, is to be atoned for, if a man is killed, with six half marks, and if no one is killed, with twelve ores.

Und der Friedensschutz, der gegeben wird im Gericht Einer Stadt, den büsse man mit 6 Hundert; und der im Wapentake gegeben wird, den büsse man mit 1 Hundert, wenn man ihn bricht; und der im Bierhause gegeben wird, den büsse man, [wenn man da] einen Menschen erschlagen, mit 6 Halbmark, und [wenn Angegriffener] lebt, mit 12 Ör.

And the protection which is given in the court of a single borough, let it be compensated with 6 hundred; and that which is given in the wapentake, let it be compensated with 1 hundred, if it is broken; and that which is given in an alehouse, let it be compensated, [if] a person [is] killed [there], with 6 half-marks, and [if the person attacked] lives, with 12 ores.
div.note: H's ‘burhgaþinðe’ (with I written above ‘ga’ by the scribe) is emended by editors to ‘burhgeþincðe’; ‘þær’ should be ‘þæt’, but the archetype had ‘þær’ (Quadr.).
i.e. whether anyone is killed or not
A mark consists of eight ores.
